schema_lineage.purpose: Evaluate vendors providing offensive security, continuous threat exposure management (CTEM), vulnerability management, and application security testing capabilities. Assesses attack surface management, vulnerability prioritization, offensive testing automation, DevSecOps integration, remediation lifecycle, AI adoption maturity, and pricing model sophistication.

offensive_security_taxonomy_v1.0.intent: Assess offensive security vendor capability alignment across five capability pillars and a separate pricing model evaluation scale. The capability assessment spans attack surface discovery through automated offensive testing, application security integration, and closed-loop remediation lifecycle management. AI maturity is evaluated as a cross-cutting dimension, with particular emphasis on agentic AI adoption in automated testing, exposure prioritization, and DevSecOps pipeline integration. The pricing model assessment evaluates commercial construct maturity using an adapted version of Gartner's composable pricing framework. Vendors are evaluated on demonstrated, publicly verifiable capability, not marketing claims.

metadata.framework_alignment: Gartner CTEM Framework + MITRE ATT&CK + OWASP + NIST CSF 2.0 + NIST SSDF + CVE/CVSS/EPSS + Gartner Composable Pricing Research (G00826132 / G00846386)

capability_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of capability in this area

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No publicly verifiable evidence of capability in this sub-pillar.
scoring_logic.1: Minimal: Basic or manual capability; no automation, analytics, or continuous operation.
scoring_logic.2: Generic Claims: Marketing mentions the capability but lacks named products, technical docs, metrics, or specifics.
scoring_logic.3: Demonstrated: Documented capability with named products or features, some technical detail, and identifiable use cases.
scoring_logic.4: Advanced: Named products with measurable outcomes, integration points, customer validation, or analyst recognition. Automation and continuous operation present.
scoring_logic.5: Market-Leading: Best-in-class capability with deep technical evidence, extensive customer base, analyst leadership recognition, measurable impact metrics, and continuous innovation.

pricing_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of this pricing construct

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No public information available about this pricing dimension.
scoring_logic.1: Opaque: Pricing exists but is entirely opaque, no public detail on structure, components, or methodology.
scoring_logic.2: Basic: General pricing information available but limited transparency, bundled quotes without component breakdown.
scoring_logic.3: Structured: Defined pricing structure with identifiable components, documented on website or in sales materials.
scoring_logic.4: Transparent & Flexible: Clear component-based pricing with published tiers, calculators, or configurators. Demonstrated client flexibility.
scoring_logic.5: Composable Best Practice: Fully composable pricing model with transparent subscription, usage, fixed, and success-fee components. Real-time usage dashboards, documented KPI alignment, and demonstrated risk-sharing mechanisms.

source_policy.description: Evidence must be publicly accessible and verifiable.

coverage_grade.description: Letter grade based on percentage of capability sub-pillars covered (score >= 1)

offensive_security_vendor_type.Pureplay Exposure Management Platform: Vendors whose primary offering is a unified continuous threat exposure management platform spanning discovery, assessment, validation, and remediation.
offensive_security_vendor_type.Extended Security Platform: Large security vendors offering offensive security capabilities as part of a broader security suite (XDR, CNAPP, or security operations platform).
offensive_security_vendor_type.Offensive Security Specialist: Vendors focused primarily on automated penetration testing, breach and attack simulation, red team automation, or adversary emulation.
offensive_security_vendor_type.DevSecOps-Integrated: Vendors whose primary approach integrates application security testing directly into CI/CD pipelines and the software development lifecycle.
offensive_security_vendor_type.Vulnerability Management Specialist: Vendors focused primarily on vulnerability scanning, assessment, and risk-based prioritization across infrastructure and applications.

deployment_model.SaaS-Only: Cloud-delivered platform with no on-premises deployment option.
deployment_model.Hybrid: Supports both cloud-delivered and on-premises or agent-based deployment.
deployment_model.On-Premises: Primarily deployed within the customer's infrastructure.
deployment_model.Agent-Based: Requires deployment of agents on target systems for scanning or testing.

ASM.name: Attack Surface Management & Discovery
ASM.focus: Continuous discovery, inventory, and monitoring of an organization's complete attack surface, including external-facing assets, cloud environments, shadow IT, and internal infrastructure. Evaluates the ability to maintain a real-time, contextualized view of all assets and exposures that adversaries could target.
evidence_signals: Continuous external and internal attack surface discovery and enumeration
Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environment asset mapping and monitoring
Shadow IT, unknown asset, and subsidiary discovery capabilities
Asset classification with business context and criticality scoring
Real-time change detection and drift monitoring across the attack surface

VUL.name: Vulnerability Assessment & Prioritization
VUL.focus: Comprehensive vulnerability scanning, detection, and risk-based prioritization across infrastructure, applications, and cloud workloads. Evaluates vendor capability to move beyond CVSS-only scoring toward business-context, exploitability, and threat-intelligence-enriched prioritization that reduces noise and focuses remediation on exposures that matter.
evidence_signals: Multi-environment vulnerability scanning (infrastructure, cloud, containers, applications)
Risk-based prioritization using CVSS, EPSS, threat intelligence, and business context
Configuration assessment and compliance benchmarking (CIS, DISA STIG, NIST)
Exploitability validation and proof-of-exploit capabilities
Vulnerability intelligence correlation with active threat campaigns

OFT.name: Offensive Testing & Validation
OFT.focus: Automated and continuous offensive security testing that validates whether identified exposures are actually exploitable and measures defensive control effectiveness. Includes automated penetration testing, breach and attack simulation (BAS), red/purple team automation, attack path analysis, and adversary emulation aligned to real-world TTPs.
evidence_signals: Automated penetration testing with safe exploitation of real vulnerabilities
Breach and attack simulation (BAS) across the kill chain
Red team and purple team automation with continuous validation
Attack path analysis and modeling from initial access to critical assets
Adversary emulation aligned to MITRE ATT&CK techniques and threat actor profiles

APP.name: Application Security Testing & DevSecOps Integration
APP.focus: Security testing capabilities embedded in the software development lifecycle, from code analysis through runtime protection. Evaluates SAST, DAST, IAST, API security testing, software composition analysis, and the depth of CI/CD pipeline integration. Particular emphasis on agentic AI adoption in automated code review, vulnerability detection, and remediation suggestion within developer workflows.
evidence_signals: Static application security testing (SAST) with IDE and repository integration
Dynamic application security testing (DAST) with authenticated scanning
API security testing covering REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and WebSocket interfaces
Software composition analysis (SCA) with license and vulnerability tracking
Native CI/CD pipeline integration with policy-as-code enforcement

REM.name: Remediation, Lifecycle & Exposure Management
REM.focus: Closed-loop remediation workflow from exposure identification through verified fix, including automated patching orchestration, risk-based prioritization of remediation actions, integration with IT service management and ticketing systems, validation that fixes are effective, and executive-level reporting on exposure trends and risk posture improvement over time.
evidence_signals: Automated remediation and patching orchestration across infrastructure and applications
Risk-based remediation prioritization with SLA tracking and accountability
Integration with ITSM, ticketing, and workflow systems (ServiceNow, Jira, etc.)
Closed-loop validation and verification that remediation actions resolved the exposure
Executive dashboards and metrics tracking exposure trends, SLA compliance, and risk posture improvement

ASM-01.name: External Attack Surface Discovery
ASM-01.expanded_definition: Continuous, automated discovery of externally facing assets, services, and exposures across domains, IP ranges, cloud providers, SaaS applications, and third-party infrastructure. Includes identification of forgotten, orphaned, or misconfigured assets exposed to the internet.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated external asset discovery across domains, IPs, and cloud providers
Identification of orphaned, forgotten, and shadow assets exposed to the internet
Subdomain enumeration, certificate transparency monitoring, and DNS analysis
Third-party and supply chain attack surface visibility
Frequency and depth of discovery scans (continuous vs. periodic)

ASM-02.name: Internal Asset Inventory & Classification
ASM-02.expanded_definition: Comprehensive internal asset discovery and classification across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid infrastructure. Includes automated asset tagging with business context, ownership attribution, data sensitivity classification, and criticality scoring to support risk-based decision-making.
what_to_verify_publicly: Internal network and endpoint asset discovery and inventory
Automated asset classification by type, function, and technology stack
Business context tagging including ownership, criticality, and data sensitivity
Integration with CMDB, cloud provider APIs, and identity systems
Asset inventory accuracy and freshness metrics

ASM-03.name: Cloud & Hybrid Environment Mapping
ASM-03.expanded_definition: Deep visibility into cloud and hybrid infrastructure including IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, container environments, serverless functions, and multi-cloud deployments. Maps security group configurations, IAM policies, storage permissions, and network topology to identify cloud-specific exposures.
what_to_verify_publicly: Multi-cloud asset discovery and inventory (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI)
Container and Kubernetes cluster visibility and security posture
Serverless function enumeration and permission analysis
Cloud IAM policy analysis and privilege escalation path detection
Cloud storage and database exposure detection (S3 buckets, blob storage, etc.)

ASM-04.name: Shadow IT & Unknown Asset Detection
ASM-04.expanded_definition: Identification of unauthorized, unmanaged, or unknown technology assets operating within or connected to the organization's infrastructure. Includes rogue SaaS application detection, unauthorized cloud accounts, personal device visibility, and third-party integrations operating outside IT governance.
what_to_verify_publicly: Rogue SaaS and unauthorized cloud application detection
Unknown device and endpoint discovery on the network
Unauthorized cloud account and subscription identification
Third-party integration and API connection visibility
Alerting and workflow for bringing shadow assets under governance

ASM-05.name: Continuous Attack Surface Change Monitoring
ASM-05.expanded_definition: Real-time or near-real-time monitoring of changes to the attack surface, including new asset deployments, configuration changes, certificate expirations, DNS modifications, and exposure drift. Provides alerting on security-relevant changes and tracks attack surface growth or reduction over time.
what_to_verify_publicly: Real-time or near-real-time change detection across the attack surface
Alerting on new exposures, misconfigurations, and certificate issues
Attack surface trending and growth metrics over time
Integration with change management and DevOps deployment pipelines
Historical attack surface snapshots for comparison and audit

VUL-01.name: Vulnerability Scanning & Detection
VUL-01.expanded_definition: Comprehensive vulnerability scanning across infrastructure, operating systems, applications, network devices, cloud workloads, and containers. Includes authenticated and unauthenticated scanning, agent-based and agentless approaches, and coverage of CVE databases, vendor advisories, and zero-day disclosures.
what_to_verify_publicly: Multi-environment scanning (infrastructure, cloud, containers, applications)
Authenticated and unauthenticated scanning capabilities
Agent-based and agentless scanning deployment options
CVE database coverage, update frequency, and zero-day advisory integration
Scanning frequency options (continuous, scheduled, on-demand)

VUL-02.name: Risk-Based Vulnerability Prioritization
VUL-02.expanded_definition: Prioritization of vulnerabilities using multi-factor risk scoring that goes beyond CVSS to incorporate exploitability data (EPSS), active threat intelligence, asset criticality, business context, and environmental factors. Reduces the volume of actionable findings to focus remediation effort on exposures that present genuine risk.
what_to_verify_publicly: Multi-factor risk scoring beyond CVSS (EPSS, threat intelligence, business context)
Asset criticality and business impact integration in prioritization
Active exploitation and in-the-wild threat correlation
Reduction metrics: percentage of vulnerabilities deprioritized through context
Customizable risk scoring policies aligned to organizational risk appetite

VUL-03.name: Configuration & Compliance Assessment
VUL-03.expanded_definition: Assessment of system, application, and cloud configurations against established security baselines and compliance benchmarks. Includes CIS Benchmark validation, DISA STIG compliance, cloud provider security best practices, and custom policy enforcement with deviation tracking and remediation guidance.
what_to_verify_publicly: CIS Benchmark assessment across operating systems, databases, and cloud platforms
DISA STIG and government compliance baseline checking
Cloud provider security best practice validation (AWS, Azure, GCP)
Custom policy and configuration standard enforcement
Configuration drift detection and compliance trending over time

VUL-04.name: Exploitability Validation
VUL-04.expanded_definition: Techniques that validate whether identified vulnerabilities are actually exploitable in the target environment, moving beyond theoretical risk to proven impact. Includes safe exploit execution, proof-of-concept validation, and environmental context analysis that confirms or eliminates vulnerabilities based on compensating controls, network segmentation, or runtime protection.
what_to_verify_publicly: Safe exploit execution and proof-of-concept validation capabilities
Environmental context analysis (compensating controls, segmentation, WAF)
Differentiation between theoretically vulnerable and actually exploitable
Integration with offensive testing tools for validation workflows
False positive reduction metrics through exploitability confirmation

VUL-05.name: Vulnerability Intelligence & Threat Correlation
VUL-05.expanded_definition: Integration of vulnerability findings with active threat intelligence, exploit availability data, and attacker campaign information to identify which vulnerabilities are being actively targeted. Correlates CVEs with known threat actor toolkits, exploit-in-the-wild databases, and dark web intelligence.
what_to_verify_publicly: Threat intelligence integration with vulnerability findings
Active exploit and in-the-wild exploitation tracking (CISA KEV, etc.)
Correlation with known threat actor TTPs and campaign indicators
Dark web and exploit marketplace monitoring for vulnerability exploitation
Automated enrichment of vulnerability records with threat context

OFT-01.name: Automated Penetration Testing
OFT-01.expanded_definition: Continuous or on-demand automated penetration testing that safely exploits real vulnerabilities to demonstrate actual business impact. Includes intelligent scoping, credential harvesting, privilege escalation, lateral movement, and objective-based testing (e.g., reach domain admin, exfiltrate data) with proof of exploitation and remediation guidance.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated penetration testing with safe, real exploitation of vulnerabilities
Multi-vector testing (network, application, cloud, identity)
Objective-based testing scenarios (reach critical assets, exfiltrate data)
Credential harvesting, privilege escalation, and lateral movement simulation
Detailed remediation guidance tied to proven exploitation paths

OFT-02.name: Breach & Attack Simulation (BAS)
OFT-02.expanded_definition: Continuous simulation of known attack techniques across the full kill chain to validate that security controls detect and prevent threats as expected. Tests endpoint protection, network security, email security, web gateway, and cloud security controls against a library of attack scenarios updated with emerging threats.
what_to_verify_publicly: Kill-chain simulation covering initial access through exfiltration
Security control validation across endpoint, network, email, and cloud
Attack scenario library size, update frequency, and emerging threat coverage
Control gap identification with specific detection and prevention failures
Continuous and scheduled simulation options with drift detection

OFT-03.name: Red Team & Purple Team Automation
OFT-03.expanded_definition: Automated red team operations that replicate sophisticated adversary behavior beyond individual technique execution, including multi-stage attack campaigns, evasion techniques, and objective-driven operations. Purple team automation provides real-time collaboration between offensive testing and defensive detection to improve security posture iteratively.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated multi-stage attack campaigns replicating real adversary behavior
Evasion technique simulation (obfuscation, living-off-the-land, fileless attacks)
Purple team mode with real-time detection validation and SOC integration
Campaign replay and variation testing for defensive tuning
Customizable adversary profiles and objective-driven operations

OFT-04.name: Attack Path Analysis & Modeling
OFT-04.expanded_definition: Graph-based analysis of potential attack paths from initial access points to critical assets, identifying the highest-risk chains of vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and identity relationships that an attacker could exploit. Prioritizes remediation based on path criticality and the number of paths a single fix would eliminate.
what_to_verify_publicly: Graph-based attack path discovery from entry points to critical assets
Identity, credential, and privilege escalation path mapping
Choke point identification showing highest-impact remediation targets
Cloud and hybrid environment attack path coverage
Visualization of attack paths with risk scoring and blast radius analysis

OFT-05.name: Adversary Emulation & MITRE ATT&CK Alignment
OFT-05.expanded_definition: Emulation of specific threat actor behaviors and TTPs aligned to the MITRE ATT&CK framework to test organizational readiness against named adversary groups. Includes threat-informed testing based on sector-specific threat profiles, MITRE Engenuity ATT&CK Evaluations participation, and mapping of test results to specific techniques and sub-techniques.
what_to_verify_publicly: MITRE ATT&CK technique and sub-technique coverage in testing
Named threat actor emulation profiles (APT groups, ransomware operators)
Sector-specific threat scenarios aligned to industry threat landscape
MITRE Engenuity ATT&CK Evaluations participation and results
Mapping of test findings to specific ATT&CK techniques with detection gaps

APP-01.name: Static & Dynamic Application Security Testing (SAST/DAST)
APP-01.expanded_definition: Source code analysis (SAST) and runtime application testing (DAST) capabilities for identifying security vulnerabilities in applications. SAST analyzes source code, bytecode, or binaries without execution. DAST tests running applications by sending crafted requests. Includes IAST (Interactive AST) approaches that combine both. Evaluates language coverage, framework support, accuracy, and integration with developer workflows.
what_to_verify_publicly: SAST support across major languages and frameworks (Java, .NET, Python, JavaScript, Go, etc.)
DAST capabilities with authenticated and unauthenticated scanning
IAST integration combining code analysis with runtime observation
False positive rates and accuracy metrics or benchmarks (OWASP Benchmark)
IDE integration and developer-friendly vulnerability presentation

APP-02.name: API Security Testing
APP-02.expanded_definition: Dedicated security testing for API endpoints covering REST, GraphQL, gRPC, SOAP, and WebSocket interfaces. Includes API discovery, schema analysis, authentication and authorization testing, injection and parameter manipulation, rate limiting validation, and business logic testing specific to API architectures.
what_to_verify_publicly: API discovery and inventory across REST, GraphQL, gRPC, and WebSocket
OpenAPI/Swagger and GraphQL schema-based test generation
OWASP API Security Top 10 coverage and testing
Authentication, authorization, and BOLA/IDOR testing capabilities
Business logic and rate limiting validation for API-specific threats

APP-03.name: Software Composition Analysis (SCA)
APP-03.expanded_definition: Analysis of open-source and third-party software components, libraries, and dependencies for known vulnerabilities, license compliance issues, and supply chain risks. Includes SBOM generation, dependency graph analysis, reachability analysis (determining if vulnerable code is actually called), and monitoring of component health and maintenance status.
what_to_verify_publicly: Open-source vulnerability detection across package ecosystems (npm, Maven, PyPI, etc.)
SBOM generation and management (CycloneDX, SPDX formats)
Reachability analysis determining if vulnerable code paths are actually exercised
License compliance detection and policy enforcement
Dependency graph visualization and transitive dependency risk assessment

APP-04.name: CI/CD Pipeline Security Integration
APP-04.expanded_definition: Native integration of security testing into continuous integration and continuous deployment pipelines, enabling automated security gates, policy-as-code enforcement, and shift-left security workflows. Evaluates depth of integration with major CI/CD platforms, scan speed impact on pipeline velocity, and the ability to enforce security policies without blocking developer productivity.
what_to_verify_publicly: Native integrations with CI/CD platforms (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps)
Security gate enforcement with configurable pass/fail policies
Scan speed and pipeline impact metrics (time overhead per scan)
Policy-as-code support for security requirements (OPA, custom policies)
Developer-facing fix guidance and auto-remediation pull requests

APP-05.name: Container, IaC & Cloud-Native Application Security
APP-05.expanded_definition: Security testing for cloud-native application architectures including container image scanning, Infrastructure as Code (IaC) template analysis, Kubernetes manifest validation, serverless function security, and runtime container protection. Evaluates coverage of cloud-native attack surface and integration with cloud-native development workflows.
what_to_verify_publicly: Container image scanning in registries and CI/CD pipelines
IaC template analysis (Terraform, CloudFormation, ARM, Pulumi, Helm)
Kubernetes manifest and admission controller security validation
Serverless function security analysis and permission review
Runtime container protection and drift detection in production

REM-01.name: Automated Remediation & Patching Orchestration
REM-01.expanded_definition: Capabilities to automate or orchestrate the remediation of identified vulnerabilities and exposures, including automated patch deployment, configuration correction, and integration with endpoint management and cloud infrastructure APIs for direct remediation action. Evaluates the breadth of automated fix capabilities versus manual remediation guidance only.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated patch deployment or orchestration capabilities
Configuration auto-remediation for known misconfigurations
Integration with endpoint management tools (SCCM, Intune, Jamf, etc.)
Cloud-native remediation through provider APIs (AWS SSM, Azure Automation)
Rollback capabilities and remediation safety controls

REM-02.name: Exposure Prioritization & Risk Scoring
REM-02.expanded_definition: Unified risk scoring and prioritization engine that aggregates findings from vulnerability scanning, attack surface management, offensive testing, and application security into a single, contextualized view. Prioritizes remediation actions based on business risk, exploitability, asset criticality, and threat activity rather than raw vulnerability counts.
what_to_verify_publicly: Unified risk scoring aggregating findings across multiple security tools
Business context and asset criticality integration in prioritization
Exposure trending and risk posture scoring over time
Customizable risk policies aligned to organizational risk appetite
Reduction in remediation volume through intelligent prioritization

REM-03.name: Remediation Workflow & Ticketing Integration
REM-03.expanded_definition: Integration with IT service management (ITSM), project management, and developer workflow tools to create, assign, track, and escalate remediation tasks. Includes automated ticket creation with enriched context, SLA tracking, escalation rules, and bi-directional synchronization between the security platform and remediation workflow systems.
what_to_verify_publicly: ITSM integration (ServiceNow, Jira, Azure DevOps, BMC Remedy)
Automated ticket creation with vulnerability context and fix guidance
SLA tracking and escalation rules for overdue remediation
Bi-directional sync between security platform and ticketing system
Assignment routing based on asset ownership and team responsibility

REM-04.name: Validation & Verification (Closed-Loop Remediation)
REM-04.expanded_definition: Capabilities to verify that remediation actions successfully resolved the identified exposure, completing the closed-loop from discovery through fix to confirmation. Includes automated re-scanning, re-testing, and validation workflows that confirm vulnerability closure and detect remediation regression.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated re-scanning or re-testing after remediation to verify fix
Closed-loop workflow from finding to remediation to verification
Regression detection for previously remediated vulnerabilities
Remediation effectiveness metrics and fix rate tracking
Integration with offensive testing for post-fix validation

REM-05.name: Metrics, Reporting & Executive Dashboards
REM-05.expanded_definition: Comprehensive reporting and visualization of exposure management program effectiveness, including executive-level risk posture dashboards, operational metrics (MTTR, fix rates, SLA compliance), trend analysis, compliance reporting, and board-ready presentation of security posture improvement over time.
what_to_verify_publicly: Executive dashboards with risk posture trending and improvement metrics
Operational metrics including MTTR, fix rates, and backlog aging
SLA compliance tracking and reporting by team, business unit, or asset class
Compliance and regulatory reporting (PCI DSS, SOX, HIPAA, etc.)
Board-ready and exportable reporting formats

ai_maturity_model.description: Assessment of AI adoption maturity across offensive security capabilities, with particular emphasis on agentic AI in automated testing, exposure triage, DevSecOps integration, and remediation orchestration.

1.name: Manual / Traditional
1.description: No meaningful AI integration. Processes rely entirely on manual analysis, rule-based scanning, signature matching, and human-driven workflows. Vulnerability prioritization based on raw CVSS scores without contextual enrichment.
indicators: Rule-based and signature-only scanning
Manual vulnerability triage and prioritization
No ML or AI in detection, testing, or remediation workflows
Static playbooks and manual ticket creation

2.name: AI-Augmented
2.description: AI assists human operators in specific workflows. Machine learning enhances vulnerability prioritization, reduces false positives, or accelerates scan analysis. Human decision-making remains primary for all critical actions. AI capabilities are bolt-on features rather than architectural foundations.
indicators: ML-enhanced vulnerability prioritization beyond CVSS
AI-assisted false positive reduction in scanning results
Natural language processing for vulnerability description analysis
AI-generated remediation suggestions that humans review and execute

3.name: AI-Automated
3.description: AI drives significant portions of the workflow with human oversight. Automated triage, scanning optimization, and remediation orchestration operate continuously with human review at defined checkpoints. Named AI products or features with documented performance metrics.
indicators: Automated vulnerability triage with confidence scoring
AI-optimized scan scheduling and resource allocation
Automated remediation for well-understood vulnerability classes
AI-driven attack path analysis and exposure correlation
Documented reduction in analyst workload through AI automation

4.name: AI-Agentic
4.description: Autonomous AI agents perform complex security testing, analysis, and remediation tasks with minimal human intervention. Agents reason about attack surfaces, plan and execute multi-step testing campaigns, generate and validate exploits, and orchestrate remediation workflows. Human oversight through governance frameworks rather than per-action approval.
indicators: Autonomous penetration testing agents that plan, execute, and adapt
Agentic vulnerability research and zero-day discovery
AI agents generating and submitting remediation pull requests
Multi-agent systems coordinating discovery, testing, and remediation
Governance frameworks defining agent autonomy boundaries
Documented agent decision transparency and audit trails

5.name: AI-Native
5.description: The platform is architecturally built around AI capabilities rather than having AI layered onto traditional tools. AI is the primary decision-making engine for exposure management, with continuous self-optimization, cross-domain reasoning, and predictive exposure forecasting. Human involvement is strategic oversight rather than operational execution.
indicators: AI-native architecture where AI is the primary processing engine, not an add-on
Continuous self-optimization of testing strategies based on results
Predictive exposure forecasting before vulnerabilities are disclosed
Cross-domain AI reasoning connecting ASM, vulnerability, AppSec, and remediation data
AI-generated security policy recommendations based on organizational context
Published AI research, patents, or benchmark results demonstrating depth

pricing_evaluation.description: Evaluation of pricing model maturity for offensive security vendors, adapted from the MDR composable pricing framework. Assesses the transition from opaque, seat-based licensing toward transparent, usage-aligned, and outcome-linked pricing models. Particular focus on how AI-driven efficiency improvements are reflected in commercial terms and whether vendors share efficiency dividends with customers.

dimensions.name: Subscription & License Transparency
dimensions.description: Clarity and transparency of the vendor's subscription or license pricing structure. Evaluates whether tiers, included features, volume bands, and upgrade paths are publicly documented and understandable.
what_to_evaluate: Published pricing tiers or license structure with clear feature definitions
Component breakdown (scanning, testing, remediation, reporting) visible to buyers
Volume-based or asset-count-based pricing clarity (per-IP, per-app, per-endpoint)
Scope adjustment and scaling flexibility within the subscription model
Renewal and upgrade path transparency

dimensions.name: Usage-Based & Consumption Alignment
dimensions.description: Degree to which pricing aligns with actual usage and consumption patterns rather than fixed seats or licenses. Evaluates availability of consumption-based pricing, metered billing, and transparent usage dashboards.
what_to_evaluate: Consumption-based pricing tied to scan volume, asset count, or API calls
Real-time usage dashboards and cost tracking for customers
Overage policies and thresholds clearly defined
AI efficiency pass-through: reduced pricing when AI reduces scan or analysis time
Elastic scaling pricing aligned to project or seasonal demand

dimensions.name: Fixed & Project-Based Pricing
dimensions.description: Availability and transparency of fixed-fee or project-based pricing for discrete engagements such as penetration tests, application assessments, or compliance audits.
what_to_evaluate: Fixed-fee options for discrete engagements (pentests, assessments, audits)
Clear scope definition and deliverable specification for fixed-price work
Project vs. continuous service cost separation
Change request and scope expansion pricing processes
Milestone-based payment structures for phased engagements

dimensions.name: Success & Outcome-Based Fees
dimensions.description: Adoption of pricing models tied to measurable security outcomes rather than asset counts or time-and-materials. Evaluates whether commercial terms include risk reduction commitments, vulnerability SLA guarantees, or performance-based fee adjustments.
what_to_evaluate: Outcome metrics tied to pricing (vulnerability reduction targets, MTTR improvements)
Risk reduction guarantees or commitments with financial mechanisms
Performance-based fee adjustments (credits for unmet SLAs, bonuses for exceeded targets)
Breach warranty or financial guarantee components
Measurement methodology for outcome validation and dispute resolution

dimensions.name: Composability & Model Maturity
dimensions.description: Flexibility and modularity of the pricing model, enabling buyers to assemble service packages from independently priced components rather than purchasing monolithic bundles.
what_to_evaluate: Modular pricing for individual capabilities (ASM, VM, pentest, AppSec, remediation)
Mix-and-match service assembly without forced bundling
Budget predictability with clear per-component costs
Risk-sharing mechanisms with financial upside and downside
Pricing model flexibility across enterprise, mid-market, and SMB segments

dimensions.name: Pricing-to-Outcomes Alignment
dimensions.description: Overall alignment between what the customer pays and the measurable security outcomes delivered. Evaluates whether the pricing model creates a direct financial link between vendor revenue and customer risk reduction.
what_to_evaluate: Direct financial link between pricing and measurable risk reduction
AI efficiency gains reflected in customer pricing (pass-through economics)
Value realization metrics shared with customers to demonstrate ROI
Pricing model evolution roadmap toward outcome-based commercial terms
Avoidance of outcome-washing: pricing genuinely tied to what matters, not marketing metrics

fields.vendor_name: Full legal or trading name of the vendor
fields.primary_focus: The vendor's primary market focus area within offensive security
fields.ai_maturity_level: Current AI maturity assessment (1-5 from ai_maturity_model)

ai_pricing_influence.description: Assessment of how AI capabilities influence the vendor's pricing model and commercial construct

scale.Transformative: AI fundamentally reshapes the pricing model; outcome-based pricing is AI-dependent
scale.Significant: AI capabilities directly enable pricing differentiation (usage-based metering, outcome measurement)
scale.Emerging: AI present in product but not connected to pricing model changes
scale.Minimal: Little to no AI influence on pricing structure or commercial terms

fields.key_products: Primary product names relevant to offensive security
fields.target_market: Primary customer segment (Enterprise, Mid-Market, SMB, or All)
fields.notable_customers_or_references: Publicly referenced customers or case studies
fields.analyst_recognition: Notable analyst report inclusions (Gartner, Forrester, IDC, etc.)
